title: Your letters: Trump administration takes 'worst of worst' off Wis. streets, Tiffany says - NewsBreak
text:
By Amy Kimmes ,
6 hours ago The safety of American citizens must always come first. For too long, weak leadership in Washington allowed criminal illegal aliens to slip through the cracks and threaten our communities. That era has come to an end. Under President Trump’s leadership, the federal government is once again prioritizing public safety and removing the worst of the worst from Wisconsin’s streets.
Wisconsinites will never forget the heartbreaking Dane County crash, when Noelia Saray Martinez-Avila, a criminal illegal alien from Honduras, drove the wrong way on the highway, killing two high school sweethearts. Following DHS Secretary (Kristi) Noem’s no-nonsense approach, ICE lodged an arrest detainer on Martinez-Avila in late July, and then arrested her in mid August following state charges related to the fatal crash. While nothing can bring back these two young lives that had so much ahead of them, enforcing our laws can help prevent the next tragedy.
Just last month, ICE announced Karlett Zagal Salazar’s arrest, a criminal illegal alien from Mexico convicted of federal drug trafficking in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin. This case is emblematic of the kind of targeted public safety work that keeps lethal narcotics and violent traffickers away from Wisconsin’s kids, schools and communities.
This focus on the “worst of the worst” by DHS is not abstract. It is specific, and it is local. Take the joint operation in Manitowoc County on Sept. 25 with Customs and Border Protection coordinating with the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service, and the Drug Enforcement Administration, resulting in the arrest of 24 criminal illegal aliens with suspected ties to an international human trafficking and drug smuggling ring. Among the illegal aliens apprehended were individuals charged with or convicted of sexually assaulting a child, a hit-and-run, driving under the influence, identity theft, and possession of narcotic equipment.
These examples reflect an astonishing record of success. In October, the Department of Homeland Security announced that more than 2 million illegal aliens have left the U.S. under President Trump and Secretary Noem’s leadership, including 527,000 deportations and 1.6 million voluntary departures.
As a member of the House Judiciary Committee, I have spent years working to ensure the safety of Wisconsinites. Last Congress, I introduced an amendment to bar sanctuary jurisdictions, such as Dane County, from receiving federal funds. This Congress, I am leading legislation to prevent states from issuing driver’s licenses to illegal aliens.
Here in Wisconsin, Gov. Tony Evers has repeatedly tried to include provisions in state budgets that would grant driver’s licenses to illegal aliens. Thankfully, the Legislature has stopped him each time. However, that is not the case in our neighboring states of Illinois and Minnesota.
Recently, a criminal alien in Lisbon, Wisconsin, was charged in a hit-and-run that injured two children. To make matters worse, she was carrying a driver’s license issued by the state of Illinois. This dangerous and reckless practice must end.
That is why I joined Rep. Jodey Arrington in introducing the Stop Greenlighting Driver Licenses for Illegal Immigrants Act, which will withhold federal funds from states that continue to issue licenses to illegal aliens. Department of Transportation Sec. Sean Duffy is also taking action to crack down on this problem. Issuing driver’s licenses to illegal aliens anywhere puts American motorists at risk everywhere.
I said then, and I believe now, that it is long past time for the federal government to secure our southern border, reclaim control over immigration, and end the reckless policies that reward illegal behavior. While there is still more work to do, particularly in removing the millions of illegal aliens already here, the Trump administration has taken important steps to restore the rule of law and strengthen public safety.
Their efforts are making Wisconsin and America safer while rebuilding the foundation for a future where our borders are secure, our families are put first, and our nation’s immigration laws are enforced.
Congressman Tom Tiffany represents Wisconsin’s Seventh Congressional District.
